scoring_contract.aggregation: unweighted sum; all five axes required; no 100-point conversion or compensating failed axis

interpretation: These are proposed report behaviours and counterexamples based on observed source features. Levels 0-2 are constructed failure examples, not findings that B01-B03 earned those scores. Level 4 adds proposed robustness requirements and independent verification; this review does not award any source or system an overall grade.
scoring_rules: Assess material sufficiency within each unchanged axis, not the number of checklist items.
A missing or unobservable material input is recorded as unverified and constrains the conclusion; it is never silently scored as satisfied.
No axis waiver or redistribution. A legitimate narrow mandate must still meet all five axes for that declared purpose; a partial full-valuation attempt is not relabelled as a successful report.
Independent review completion is recorded separately; it is necessary for the proposed level 4 but never sufficient by itself.
The 14 existing criteria may be evidence prompts mapped to axes, not extra scored dimensions.

levels.label: Absent or false provenance
levels.concrete_example: A report presents the confidential SG Fleet Internal Projections or the Gold Road site work as work it obtained/performed, but has only the published PDFs; or invents a supporting page.

levels.label: Citation without decision-relevant support
levels.concrete_example: A SG Fleet forecast claim cites only the booklet title; its source list never distinguishes public history from management projections. The citation exists but does not allow the claim to be checked.

levels.label: Traceable yet materially incomplete
levels.concrete_example: The report cites SG Fleet 7.2-7.5 and 10.1, but still relies on unavailable private cash flows for a precise unconditional value, or misses the image-only Figure 39 while asserting it verified that bridge.

levels.label: Adequate traceability and bounded claims
levels.concrete_example: Each material SG Fleet claim identifies original/hash/page/table, as-of date and public/private origin. Missing private forecasts and extraction gaps are explicit; original images support quoted figures. Conclusions are restricted to what that evidence supports.

levels.label: Strong challenge and reconciled evidence
levels.concrete_example: Meets 3, plus a separate reviewer checks the exact claim-to-original chain, challenges contrary evidence (including the peer-comparability caveat in SG Fleet footnote 30), reconciles discrepancies and records residual uncertainty and its effect on the decision. Hashes alone or a reviewer name do not earn 4.

levels.label: Economically contradicted
levels.concrete_example: Apply an enterprise WACC to SG Fleet real geared equity cash flows without conversion, or value the finite Gold Road production assets as an undifferentiated perpetual earnings stream.

levels.label: Generic method with unsupported economics
levels.concrete_example: Insert a standard DCF and arbitrary terminal growth; copy management fleet growth and synergy assumptions without testing orders, deliveries, residual income or funding needs.

levels.label: Recognised drivers, unresolved material premise
levels.concrete_example: Identify the fleet pipeline, EOL income and advance-rate risks but leave perpetual deliveries above orders, unexplained terminal reinvestment, or incompatible funding assumptions in the base case.

levels.label: Mandate-specific coherent economics
levels.concrete_example: Use operating evidence to normalise deliveries/orders and EOL income, test synergy timing and achievable funding, and connect terminal margins/growth to equity reinvestment. Explain why real equity flows require a real equity discount rate; for finite assets justify the separate residual-resource treatment.

levels.label: Robust economics under credible alternatives
levels.concrete_example: Meets 3, plus an independent challenge quantifies interacting downside drivers, reconciles method differences and ownership/financing allocation, and demonstrates which evidence supports or changes the selected range. Explain why the unsupported EOL upside or extra synergies are not the central case; justify range selection rather than copying the published range.

levels.label: Materially wrong calculation or scope
levels.concrete_example: Use SG Fleet Figure 39 A$000 as A$m, discount equity flows and subtract debt again, or materially misstate the TPG-to-HTAL ownership bridge.

levels.label: Reported answer with no reconstruction
levels.concrete_example: Copy HTAL or SG Fleet endpoints and per-share values into a polished table with no source-linked arithmetic, dilution schedule or sign convention.

levels.label: Partial reconciliation, material unresolved issue
levels.concrete_example: Recompute the HTAL subtotal but mechanically deduct the positive other-balance-sheet amount because the row label says Less; or reproduce a nominal WACC but use it as real. Other arithmetic passing does not cure the open error.

levels.label: Reproducible calculation for the stated scope
levels.concrete_example: Reperform the disclosed bridges with original units, signs, ownership, cash-flow basis and diluted shares; separate displayed rounding from unexplained differences. Distinguish Deloitte calculated real WACC from its selected WACC and flag unavailable private-model reconstruction.

levels.label: Independent end-to-end and stress reconciliation
levels.concrete_example: Meets 3, plus a separate reviewer independently rebuilds material report outputs from the accessible approved inputs, tests perturbations and boundary cases, and ties charts, prose and tables to one frozen model. For a full valuation, public summary arithmetic alone cannot earn 4; missing model support restricts the output.

levels.label: Wrong question or unsupported conclusion
levels.concrete_example: Call an offer attractive merely because its price exceeds a historical quotation, apply the Australian transaction test to a different mandate without justification, or claim the unvalued SG Fleet scrip is fair.

levels.label: Conclusion with generic risk list
levels.concrete_example: State a fair value and list commodity, execution and liquidity risks, without explaining the intended shareholder decision, alternatives or how any risk changes the recommendation.

source_locators.section: Summary and conclusion; Table 1 and note

levels.label: Relevant analysis without resolving the choice
levels.concrete_example: Show Gold Road sensitivities or SG Fleet scenarios, but never explain selected versus rejected cases, no-deal consequences, or the limits of a cash-versus-scrip comparison.

levels.label: Supported choice with a credible contrary case
levels.concrete_example: Name the reader, interest and test; link the conclusion to value evidence, no-deal alternatives and a material contrary argument such as SG Fleet holders surrendering future synergy upside. Preserve its explicit inability to estimate scrip reliably and the Gold Road valuation-date qualification.

source_locators.section: Summary and conclusion; Table 1 and note

levels.label: Decision remains accountable under changing evidence
levels.concrete_example: Meets 3, plus quantitatively identify the material change that could reverse or qualify the recommendation, explain range-selection judgment and dependent cross-checks, and specify the evidence/update or action the decision-maker needs. An independent reviewer challenges the strongest contrary case. These additions are candidate requirements, not claims that every source demonstrates all of them.

levels.label: Unusable or misleading exhibit
levels.concrete_example: A final report drops SG Fleet Figure 39 values, loses low/high headings or unit labels, clips a material limitation, or draws a chart whose sign/axis reverses the finding.

levels.label: Cosmetic polish without an analytical reading path
levels.concrete_example: Use professional colours and a long executive summary, but detach charts from their assumptions and sources, remove comparable-company footnotes, and leave the key decision buried.

levels.label: Mostly readable, materially incomplete communication
levels.concrete_example: Tables are sourced and readable yet flatten SG Fleet Figure 47 into an unlabeled list, omit the associated concluded range, or omit Deloitte Table 16 emphasis and interpretation; the reader cannot connect the analysis to the conclusion.

levels.label: Expert can trace the argument and exhibits
levels.concrete_example: Provide conclusion-first navigation, informative headings, table/figure IDs and cross-references, visible units/period/perimeter/basis, legible notes and a nearby interpretation. Preserve the scenario-to-range relationship and reconcile every quoted endpoint to its exhibit. Inspect the final rendered document.

levels.label: Publication-ready analytical communication
levels.concrete_example: Meets 3, plus independently inspect every final page and all material charts/tables at normal reading size, test PDF/search/accessibility where required, and verify executive conclusions/limitations against the body. Use strong visual hierarchy and compact exhibits to expose the real analytical tradeoff; brand, length or a screenshot checklist cannot substitute.
